concerns.text: T010 (Power Simulation) depends on T009 (Phase 0 Data Stub Generator) which generates synthetic data. However, T009 is marked [P] and placed in Phase 2, while T010 is also in Phase 2. The dependency T009 -> T010 is valid, but T010 also requires the 'Holm-Bonferroni correction' logic (FR-008) which is implemented in T035 (Phase 5). T010 cannot execute the required correction logic before T035 is implemented, creating a circular dependency or a missing prerequisite for T010.

T022 (Baseline Data Collection Pipeline) claims to orchestrate 'simulated real data' from T019.1. T019.1 (Pilot Check) depends on T014.1 (Local Web Interface Wrapper). T014.1 depends on T011.1 (Static Web Interface Bundle). T011.1 is in Phase 2. The chain T011.1 -> T014.1 -> T019.1 -> T022 is logically sound, BUT T014.1 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) while it explicitly depends on the output of T011.1. If T011.1 is not completed before T014.1 starts, T014.1 cannot run. The [P] tag is misleading if it implies independence from T011.1's completion.

T034 (Wilcoxon Fallback) is described as triggering ONLY if T034.1 (Convergence Detector) detects failure. T034.1 is listed *after* T034 in the task list (T034.1 appears after T034 in the text flow, though numbered sequentially). More critically, T034.1 description says 'MUST explicitly return a flag... to trigger T034'. This implies T034.1 must run *before* T034. The current ordering in Phase 5 lists T034.1 *after* T034 (T034 is listed, then T034.1 is listed below it? No, T034.1 is listed before T034 in the provided text: 'T034.1... T034...'). Wait, looking at the text: T034.1 is listed BEFORE T034. This is correct. However, T034.1 depends on the 'bootstrap' logic (T033) to detect convergence. T033 is listed before T034.1. This is fine. BUT, T034.1 description says 'MUST explicitly forbid Shapiro-Wilk triggers'. This is a logic constraint, not an ordering one. The real issue is T034.1 depends on T033 (Bootstrap) to run. T033 is before T034.1. This is OK. The issue is T034 (Wilcoxon) depends on T034.1. T034.1 is before T034. This is OK. The real issue is T034.1 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but it depends on T033's output. If T033 is not finished, T034.1 cannot run. The [P] tag is incorrect if it implies T034.1 can run in parallel with T033.

T006.1 (register_participant) is marked [P] but depends on T006 (ID Generator) to generate IDs. If T006 is not completed, T006.1 cannot assign IDs. The [P] tag is misleading as it implies independence from T006.

T017, T018, T019 (Unit tests) are marked [P] and depend on T013 (Synthetic Data Generator) and T014/T015/T016 (Scoring functions). T013 is in Phase 3, T014-016 are in Phase 3. The tests depend on the implementation of the scorers. If the scorers are not implemented, the tests cannot run. The [P] tag is acceptable if it means 'tests can run in parallel with each other', but the description 'runs against data from T013' implies T013 must be complete. This is a minor semantic issue with the [P] tag definition in this context.
